text:
Alex: pulled an nsys capture from the failing dedicated run — timeline shows repeated small cudaMalloc/cudaFree bursts between cublasLtMatmul launches, and long idle gaps in the stream. looks like launch serialization due to workspace allocation
Monica: can you paste the nsys summary? which stream IDs are we seeing the gaps on?
Alex: here's the trimmed output from the GPU timeline (nsys):
```
GPU Timeline (stream 7):
0.000 - cublasLtMatmul (algo 7) 1.28ms
0.002 - cudaMalloc 0.92ms
0.003 - cublasLtMatmul (algo 7) 1.30ms
0.005 - cudaFree 0.12ms
0.005 - <idle> 7.84ms  <-- big gap
0.013 - cublasLtMatmul (algo 7) 1.25ms
```

Also allocator debug: slab_alloc: requested=125829120, avail_contig=65536000, alloc_fallback=1, frag_pct=47
Raj: that frag_pct is the smoking gun — algo 7 needs ~120MB workspace, our allocator only returned ~62MB contiguous, so we fall back to cudaMalloc each call (hence the serialisation)
Jess: CV: this explains the +20% P99 regression on the latest runtime build; perf-bot posted a regression alert last night
perf-bot: perf-reg: matmul_p99 +23% vs baseline build 1769801111, alloc-fallbacks increased by 4.2x, GPU occupancy unchanged
Monica: interesting it only shows up under medium batch sizes (batch 8 to 16). large batches use a different algo with larger ws but we pre-reserve for that path so no mallocs there
Alex: hypothesis: KV cache growth during generation shards memory across streams -> increases fragmentation -> small allocations fail to produce contiguous blocks so cublasLt falls back to slower path (cudaMalloc per kernel)
Raj: can repro locally with microbench: allocate random sized kv-cache slabs between runs to fragment, then run a sequence of matmuls using algos [0,1,7,11] and measure alloc_fallback_count and latency
Jess: quick mitigation options: 1) force cublasLt algo selection to prioritize no-ws algos when contiguous free < threshold, 2) maintain per-stream scratch slab pool (reserve 128MB), 3) do periodic slab defragmentation / coalescing during quiet windows
Monica: cost/complexity matrix: (1) is cheapest and quick but may hit quality/throughput for some shapes; (2) is medium complexity but predictable; (3) is higher risk but could improve long-term fragmentation
Alex: ran an experiment toggling heuristic (1) — pinned to algo 0 if avail_contig < 100MB. result: cudaMalloc calls dropped ~92%, P99 dropped back near baseline for the test prompt set, but token throughput dropped 5% on long sequences
Raj: ok we need a reproducible perf test and a telemetry change: log workspace allocation reason (fast-path vs fallback) + contig_avail on allocation failures; add counters per-model-version and per-stream
Monica: agree. action items:
- Alex: re-run nsys with slab defrag enabled (branch: slab/defrag-ws) and attach full capture + timeline (due EOD)
- Raj: add microbench sweep for algos+ws sizes and produce a CSV (due tomorrow)
- Jess: add heuristic toggle to runtime flags and run smoke on dedicated (due tomorrow)
Alex: also note: cublasLt algo fallback list includes some algos that are 0-ws but slower. we should update model catalog recommendations to include 'prefer low-ws algos under mem-pressure' guidance
Monica: I'll add a short doc to product/infra runbook and a console alert that flags "workspace fallback > 1%" for a model; helpful for customers on Dedicated
perf-bot: noted. creating ticket PERF-1723 with summary and attaching the nsys trace link
Jess: thanks — looks actionable. will follow up on regressions board once Raj's microbench lands
Alex: fwiw the capture also shows a few kernels that serialize on the same CUDA event (we didn't expect that) — might be an unrelated stream synchronization bug. I'll open a separate thread if it reproduces consistently
Monica: great, thanks team :thumbsup:
